# thonny-ai

> thonny-ai is an MCP server and a plugin for the Thonny Python IDE. It lets AI coding assistants
> (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, any MCP client over stdio) program MicroPython boards such as
> the Raspberry Pi Pico / Pico W and ESP32: run code, deploy a project, watch a long-running program's
> output, manage files. Everything the AI does is shown in Thonny's shell and logged in an
> "AI Assistant" panel, with optional approval of each action. MIT license.

Key facts:

- Install into Thonny: `pip install git+https://github.com/AstroQuestStudio/thonny-ai` from Thonny's
  "Tools → Open system shell…", or download the Windows portable build from the Releases page.
- MCP server command: `<Thonny's python> -m thonny_ai_mcp` (no dependency besides pyserial).
- MCP tools: status, info, exec, start, monitor, interrupt, stop, run_file, ls, read, write, rm,
  sync, pull, reset, shell, open, i2c_scan, gpio.
- Robots: `stop` interrupts and runs the `safe_stop` code from `.thonny-ai.json` (motors off); `monitor`
  takes `until` (regex) to wait for a line; `sync` takes `ignore` and `delete`; output per call is capped.
- Use `exec` for short code, `start` + `monitor` + `interrupt` for programs that loop forever
  (robots, sensor streams), `sync` to upload a folder (only changed files, SHA-256).
- When Thonny is open, calls go through its plugin (HTTP on 127.0.0.1:47821). When Thonny is closed,
  the server uses the board's serial port directly (MicroPython raw REPL).
- On a Raspberry Pi Pico W the onboard LED is `machine.Pin("LED")`.
- If an action returns "denied by the user", the user refused it in Thonny's approval panel.
